predecessors.name: Chalukyas of Badami
predecessors.text: the northern regions of the Chalukya empire, taken from Kirtivarman II

successors.name: Western Chalukya Empire
successors.text: the Rashtrakuta core, taken by Tailapa II when he 'dethroned Karka' in 973

successors.name: Western Ganga dynasty
successors.text: Indra IV's remnant in Ganga country

ledger.x: 753: Dantidurga defeats the Badami Chalukya army and takes the north of the Chalukya empire.
757: Krishna I defeats Kirtivarman II, the last Badami Chalukya emperor.
757: Krishna I takes Gangavadi from the Western Gangas.
757: Krishna I defeats the Shilaharas of South Konkan.
772: the east to Kalinga.
772: the east to Kosala.
772: the Srisailam country.
784: Dhruva humbles the Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana IV; a marriage alliance follows (Jetvai grant, 786).
785: Dhruva campaigns to Kanchi and the Pallava Nandivarman II accepts Rashtrakuta suzerainty.
785: the Tripartite Struggle begins and Dhruva marches north.
785: Dhruva reaches the Ganga-Yamuna country.
790: Dhruva returns to the South.
790: the Doab is left.
800: Govinda III's northern campaign.
800: Dharmapala and Chakrayudha submit to Govinda III.
800: the Kannauj campaign over; no later date on the page.
805: the Pallava tribute ends.
806: Lata (Gujarat) passes from the Pratiharas.
813: Govinda III makes his brother Indra ruler of Lata.
814: Govinda III's reign ends and the Rashtrakuta threat lapses.
814: Amoghavarsha I takes the throne and the court moves to Manyakheta.
816: the Ganga feudatory revolts.
819: Gangavadi leaves the direct land.
819 (bridge): the Gangas are Rashtrakuta feudatories from the peace of Amoghavarsha I.
821: the revolts ended.
850: Kalinga (Odisha) drops out of Cliopatria's shape.
850: Kosala (Chhattisgarh) drops out of Cliopatria's shape; no page opened says who took it, so nobody.
850: the Srisailam country drops out of Cliopatria's shape (33,636 km2); no page opened says who took it.
850: the Eastern Chalukya feudatory is gone from the Rashtrakuta shape; the page does not say how the relation ended.
860: Gujarat leaves the Rashtrakuta shape for the Pratiharas.
860 (moved from 888): the Gujarat branch tint ends where the Pratihara shape takes the land.
916: Indra III takes Kannauj.
926: Kannauj is back in Pratihara hands.
944: Krishna III secures Tondaimandalam from the Cholas.
944: war with the Cholas over Kanchi and Tanjore (Siddalingamadam plates of 944).
949: Takkolam.
967: Tondaimandalam is not Rashtrakuta after Krishna III.
973: Tailapa II takes the Deccan.
973: the Rashtrakuta remnant stands in Gangavadi.
982 (bridge): Rashtrakuta overlordship ends with Indra IV.
982: Indra IV ends his life at Shravanabelagola and the Rashtrakuta line ends.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta overthrow of the Badami Chalukyas
wars.outcome: Dantidurga defeated Kirtivarman II's army in 753 (Samangadh plate) and took the north; Krishna I defeated Kirtivarman II, 'the last Badami Chalukya emperor', in 757.

wars.name: Tripartite struggle for Kannauj
wars.outcome: Dhruva beat Vatsaraja and Dharmapala and went home in 790; Govinda III beat Nagabhata II near Gwalior and received the submission of Chakrayudha and Dharmapala (800).

wars.name: Rashtrakuta wars with the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi
wars.outcome: Dhruva humbled Vishnuvardhana IV in 784 and made a marriage alliance (786); Amoghavarsha I's war at Vingavalli is undated; Vishnuvardhana V was killed in 846; by 850 Cliopatria's shape has lost Vengi.

wars.name: Dhruva's expedition to Kanchi
wars.outcome: 'He undertook campaigns to Kanchi in 785'; the Pallava Nandivarman II was forced to accept Rashtrakuta suzerainty (undated).

wars.name: Western Ganga wars and the revolts against Amoghavarsha I
wars.outcome: Dhruva's campaign against the Western Gangas in 788; the Ganga feudatory revolt in which Shivamara II was killed in 816, further revolts 818-820 and the empire 're-established by 821'.

wars.name: Indra III's northern campaign
wars.outcome: Kannauj was 'completely destroyed' and held 'until c.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta-Chola war (Takkolam)
wars.outcome: Krishna III captured Kanchi and Tanjore (plates of 944), secured Tondaimandalam and 'in c.

wars.name: Paramara sack of Manyakheta and Tailapa's seizure
wars.outcome: In 972 the Paramara Siyaka 'invaded and sacked' Manyakheta; in 973 Tailapa II 'dethroned Karka and established a new dynasty'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is recorded on the pages opened; the northern raids, the Gujarat branch and the Vengi, Kanchi and Malwa feudatories are approximate throughout.
